title: Latency Budget Controller for Prefill/Decode with Kernel Probing
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Implement a runtime-level controller that enforces per-request latency budgets by dynamically splitting prefill and decode work, probing available kernels, and applying a lightweight weighted-fairness allocator across QoS tiers. Goal is to reduce p95/p99 end-to-end latency regressions under mixed workload while preserving acceptable throughput. Controller will: 1) accept a latency_budget_ms signal from the router or derive one from route SLOs, 2) probe candidate kernels (fp16/4-bit optimized kernels) and local attention fast-paths for short vs long sequences, 3) decide a split point between prefill and decode phases (micro-slicing) to meet the budget, 4) apply a proportional share allocator so urgent low-latency requests get prioritized without starving background throughput work, and 5) emit detailed telemetry for offline tuning and for Redwood Console dashboards. This ticket covers design, implementation, and an initial canary rollout in the eu-west region for text-generation routes.
acceptance_criteria: Controller integrates with scheduler and can receive a per-request latency_budget_ms field
End-to-end p95 latency for mixed test workload improves by at least 20% compared to baseline under same throughput targets
Kernel probing decision reproduces within 5% across repeated runs for identical request profiles
No request starvation: throughput for background batch-level traffic stays within 10% of baseline under sustained load
Telemetry exposed to Console: chosen kernel, split_point, slot_allocations, latency_budget_ms, observed_latency_ms
notes: 2025-03-06: Spike complete. Wrote microbench harness that runs kernel probes across A100 and H100 replicas. Observed that for short prefixes (<128 tokens) a small-attention kernel reduces prefill latency 30% but increases per-token decode overhead for long decodes.

2025-03-07: Design review with PM and SRE. Decided to surface latency_budget_ms from route config and allow router to override based on customer SLA. SRE requested soft-fallback policy to avoid cascading capacity thrash.
2025-03-09: Prototype controller implemented in runtime/arbiter. Added feature-flag gate and a no-op path. Early unit tests for probing logic pass locally.

2025-03-10: Perf run on canary pool: mixed load (50% short chat, 50% long generation). p95 improved by 18% but p99 unchanged. Trade-off: throughput dropped 7% for long-batch tasks. Need to tune fairness weights.

2025-03-11: Code review feedback from Priya S. and Ethan K.: request API should include 'prefer_low_latency' boolean to simplify router decision logic; add metric for kernel_probe_time_ms to track overhead; add guardrail to disable probing if probe latency > 5ms.

2025-03-12: Action items: implement 'prefer_low_latency' flag, add probing timeout and cache probe results per model+hardware+sequence_bucket, run larger perf matrix across sequence lengths [16,64,128,512]. Assigned follow-ups and set up canary rollout plan in Confluence.
